VERDICT: CLEAN
BOUNDARY: The proof handles empty K separately (step 1.2) and uses the empty-subfamily alternative for compactness. Zero-length source intervals are allowed (step 3.1), and the geometric budget from index 0 is included. A one-member subcover is possible when K is nonempty (step 4.1). Degenerate source intervals are enlarged to open intervals with positive radius. The transition from open enlargements back to closed intervals preserves the cover. The choice of a specific null cover for a given epsilon and the extraction of a finite subcover are valid. Both directions of the biconditional are proved: the forward direction is immediate from lem-content-zero-implies-null; the reverse direction is the main argument. All boundary cases are correctly addressed.
SOURCES: All 26 cited items were provided in full and inspected. Their definitions, statements, and working forms align with the uses in the target. No source mismatch was found.
